title: Conservation note for the Bell Street exchange board
public_context: A conservator's treatment note accompanies a decommissioned telephone exchange panel and an old circuit diagram. The setting includes a wooden cabinet, metal tags and paper records, within a museum or archive collection of communications equipment. The record sits with other municipal apparatus files.
source_title: Treatment record 4 for the Bell Street exchange panel
source_text:
The Bell Street panel arrived with its wooden cabinet intact and the rear cover detached. A folded circuit diagram had been tucked behind the lower rail. The drawing labels two spring contacts as North and Market, but the metal tags on the panel read Market and Quarry. Conservator Leth Arin photographed the tags before moving the diagram and placed the paper in a polyester sleeve beside the cabinet rather than flattening its old fold.

The panel had no power cable and was not connected to a working exchange. Arin did not energize the contacts. Instead, she used a blunt wooden probe to see which springs moved when a key was pressed. The key marked North moved the contact tagged Market, while the key marked Market moved the contact tagged Quarry. The key marked Quarry moved a contact with no metal tag at all. The report calls these observed movements, not proof of the original line assignments, because the diagram may describe an earlier arrangement.

A pale rectangle on the cabinet's inside wall shows where another instruction card once sat. The card itself was not found. Arin compared the screw holes with the detached rear cover and found that the cover had been attached with a different pair of screws at some point. She did not infer that the missing card was removed during that alteration. A paper strip inside the cabinet lists three dates in different inks, but none has a matching technician signature. The strip was photographed in place and not detached.

The treatment plan is limited to stabilizing the loose rear cover and housing the diagram with the panel. Arin will not repaint the keys or replace the metal tags, even where their names disagree with the diagram. The archive approved a transparent support under the detached cover so visitors can see the old screw holes. Arin marked the position of the missing card on the treatment drawing and left a blank space beside the three dates for a later curator's note. Her final observation is that the mismatch belongs to the object's history, not a defect that can be corrected from the surviving pieces alone.
